## About the trip

This is a private trip. Tours in Rio and Iguazu are led by an English-speaking guide, and English-speaking guides also work in the Pantanal and Bonito. Transfers connect the regions, while the programme in the Pantanal centres on wildlife watching and nature walks.

The route stands out for its variety. Over 13 days, you move from a Carnival night and big-city panoramas to the roaring waters of Iguazu, then to the wetlands and savannas of the Pantanal, the karst landscapes of Bonito and the peaceful ocean coast.

## How the journey changes

The first 3 days are devoted to Rio. The programme here centres on city panoramas and Carnival. Sugar Loaf reveals the coastline and bay, Corcovado offers a view from the opposite direction, and a night at the Sambadrome completely changes the pace of the trip. The move to Iguazu feels especially striking after this: the metropolis gives way to a national park and water.

At Iguazu, you visit both sides of the falls. On the Brazilian side, the sweeping panorama makes the biggest impression. On the Argentine side, the route offers a closer look: the Lower and Upper Circuits reveal the cascades from different heights, and a separate route leads to the Devil’s Throat. This gives the falls 2 full days rather than a brief stop.

The next part of the route focuses on Brazil’s inland natural regions. In the Pantanal, early outings and wildlife watching are central to the experience. In Bonito, forest walks are joined by waterfalls, caves and clear rivers. Estancia Mimosa combines a forest walk with swimming beside waterfalls, while the Rio Sucuri lets you discover the underwater world without advanced diving training.

The final transfer to Búzios brings you back to the ocean. After early outings, flights and nature excursions, you have a free day here. You can spend it actively, choosing a buggy ride, boat trip, snorkelling or water sports, or devote it entirely to the beach and relaxation.

Domestic flights connect the distant parts of the route: after Rio, you fly to Iguazu, then continue via Campo Grande to the Pantanal and Bonito, before returning to Rio after the nature-focused part of the trip and heading to the coast. The programme is designed as one continuous journey, with each region noticeably different from the last.
